opportunities.title: Leave-one-footprint-out disagreement as a common-wrong-alias diagnostic for selective UAV localization
opportunities.question: Does the shift in an accepted pose when each overlapping reference footprint is removed predict wrong-building or wrong-tile acceptance better than dispersion, residual and inlier scores, once those scores are held fixed?
opportunities.hypothesis: Inference: when several retrieved references overlap, a pose that depends on one footprint or on a shared wrong structure changes more under leave-one-footprint-out recomputation than a well-supported pose does. The shift therefore adds failure-ranking information beyond RIC-Loc-style dispersion and residual scores. This is a ranking claim only, not a calibrated posterior and not an OCI-equivalent covariance.
opportunities.contribution: Test whether a leave-one-footprint-out pose-shift statistic, computed over overlapping reference footprints, adds incremental AUROC and risk-coverage value over dispersion, residual and inlier-count scores. Inclusion criterion: stress queries made by deleting the true gallery entry.

prior_art.overlap: It already provides failure-ranking via dispersion/covariance scores, risk-coverage evaluation and a common-mode scale term. It also admits that hypotheses sharing a VGGT pass are treated as independent.
prior_art.difference: The proposed statistic uses geographic footprint overlap among references, not a shared network pass. It is evaluated only as an increment over RIC-Loc-style scores. RIC-Loc is the strongest baseline, and it needs posed references.

prior_art.overlap: OCI already treats overlapping sources as partially correlated and gives a conservative fusion construction.
prior_art.difference: No OCI covariance, zero-mean or linear-measurement assumptions are claimed. A common wrong alias is a biased error, so this is an empirical diagnostic and not a fusion law.

prior_art.overlap: RIM states it has no calibrated reject option and proposes confidence fusion as future work. Its Appendix E shows that solver output can be finite but wrong.
prior_art.difference: This candidate tests one narrow signal and does not claim a full confidence estimator.

opportunities.novelty_basis: No global novelty is claimed. The narrower claim is that footprint-overlap leave-one-out pose shift gives incremental failure-ranking information beyond dispersion and residual scores. This could be redundant with existing scores, as T09 notes.
evidence_gaps: RIC-Loc cached hypotheses and the VGGT/MegaLoc environment are unavailable (O1 prerequisite blocked).
Deleting the true gallery entry is only a stress test, not realistic temporal map change.
Whether footprint overlap tracks error dependence is unmeasured.
Prior art outside the supplied corpus was not searched.
opportunities.feasibility: Feasible only if the blocked prerequisites resolve. Otherwise, the fallback is a CPU pilot on stored retrieval/pose outputs from any available pipeline, such as RIM or OrthoLoC, using the same statistic.

experiment.hypothesis: Adding the leave-one-out pose-shift feature to dispersion, residual and inlier-count scores raises failure-detection AUROC and lowers selective risk.
datasets: Stored outputs for OrthoLoC pairs or any available posed-reference set with cached top-K candidates
Stress split: true reference removed, with a random-removal control
baselines: Combined baseline using logistic regression on the three
experiment.config: Fix K=5 and the failure threshold (position error >5 m) before looking at results. Use scene-grouped cross-validation, with the same logistic model plus or minus the new feature. Bootstrap by scene, 1000 resamples.
experiment.success: Preregistered gate: the feature adds >=0.03 AUROC with a bootstrap 95% CI lower bound >0, and lowers risk at 80% coverage by >=10% relative, on both the natural and the stress split.
experiment.falsification: Stop and report a null result if the AUROC gain is <0.01, if the CI includes 0 on the stress split, or if the Spearman correlation with dispersion is >0.9 and the gain is <0.02.
experiment.compute: CPU only, an estimated <=4 hours if hypotheses are cached. Not measured.

opportunities.title: Scene-model-violation diagnostic: homography versus DSM-lifted fit disagreement
opportunities.question: Does the disagreement between a quasi-planar homography fit and a DSM-lifted PnP fit on the same matches detect tall-structure, parallax or occlusion failures better than inlier residuals?
opportunities.hypothesis: Inference: where a single plane is violated, the homography-implied and DSM-lifted poses diverge even when RANSAC inlier ratios look healthy. That divergence should rank failures better than the inlier residual. Localized failures should then be separable from semantic-identity failures.
opportunities.contribution: Test a cheap two-model disagreement score in local coordinates, using the two existing OrthoLoC pipeline fits. Inclusion criterion: samples with at least 20% covisibility, as the source requires.

prior_art.overlap: Both fits already exist: AdHoP quasi-planar preconditioning and DSM-elevation lifting to PnP. It is the strongest named source, and it reports failure on corrupted matches.
prior_art.difference: It does not use disagreement between the two fits as a validity score. It also has not tested whether that score beats inlier residuals.

prior_art.overlap: It reports planar-homography breakdown with tall structures and parallax. It also predicts per-pixel confidence, which is a required baseline.
prior_art.difference: The diagnostic is training-free and operates on matches, but it does not produce dense geodetic output.

prior_art.overlap: Analytic photogrammetric covariance propagation already exists.
prior_art.difference: Disagreement is a model-validity signal, not a propagated covariance. It must be compared with analytic propagation if feasible.

opportunities.novelty_basis: The narrow claim is about the estimator-disagreement signal for scene-model violation. Novelty is not claimed. Its stated difference from the ortholoc and skyreg baselines is tentative and unverified.
evidence_gaps: No full matcher environment is verified.
No global coordinate transform is verified, so results are local-metric only.
Same-domain truth shares a reconstruction with the references.
opportunities.feasibility: Specifiable on CPU using the local-coordinate geometry diagnostic confirmed in the O2 prerequisite. Cached matches are needed, and otherwise the plan is blocked.

experiment.hypothesis: Homography/DSM pose disagreement has higher failure AUROC than the inlier residual.
datasets: OrthoLoC cross-domain arrays, stratified by relief/height
experiment.config: Failure means local-frame translation error >2 m or rotation error >5 degrees, fixed in advance. Compute the two poses from the same matches. Report all-query and eligible-only results.
experiment.success: AUROC >=0.70 and exceeds the inlier-ratio AUROC by >=0.05 with a bootstrap 95% CI lower bound >0, in the cross-domain strata.
experiment.falsification: Stop if the AUROC gain over inlier ratio is <0.02 or if the gain disappears in the tall-structure stratum.
experiment.compute: CPU, an estimated 2-6 hours given cached matches. Not measured.

opportunities.title: Evidence-selection ablation: is budgeted reference choice distinct from top-K by retrieval score?
opportunities.question: Under a fixed budget of matcher calls, does choosing references by footprint complementarity beat top-K by retrieval score in accepted-pose risk, or does it collapse into the same candidates?
opportunities.hypothesis: Inference: nearby overlapping tiles may repeat the same wrong structure (T09). A greedy rule that spreads selected footprints may therefore reduce correlated wrong acceptances at a fixed budget. It may also lose coverage, and it may be indistinguishable from top-K.
opportunities.contribution: Test a greedy footprint-complementarity selector under a fixed budget B against top-K, measuring both accepted-pose risk and the overlap between the two selected sets. A null or redundancy result is an acceptable outcome.

prior_art.overlap: OASIS already does budgeted subset selection with an E-optimal information objective.
prior_art.difference: It selects physical sensor mounts under independence assumptions. This candidate selects retrieved satellite references with uncertain association. No exact selector was established by the bounded search.

prior_art.overlap: It already uses a reranking-plus-PnP pipeline and proposes confidence fusion.
prior_art.difference: It reranks for accuracy and does not study how the reference set is chosen. RIM is the strongest named source.

prior_art.overlap: Geometry-aware reference selection is explicitly named as future work. It already has risk-coverage evaluation.
prior_art.difference: This is a direct attempt at that future work, so it carries a high redundancy risk.

prior_art.overlap: It already clusters candidates by 3D covisibility and uses PnP-RANSAC.
prior_art.difference: Covisibility grouping is a stronger overlap than generic hierarchy. Here the grouping is footprint-based, with no 3D map.

opportunities.novelty_basis: No novelty is claimed. The only supportable claim is a controlled comparison. It must survive classical active-localization and optimal-design prior art that was not searched here.
evidence_gaps: A non-oracle retrieval gallery is unverified.
External checkpoints and the full online runtime are unverified.
Footprint geometry is needed for each tile.
opportunities.feasibility: Marginal. It needs the released RIM weights and evaluation source (confirmed), but the non-oracle gallery is unverified. A simulated-score fallback would only test the selection logic, not the real system.

experiment.hypothesis: Complementarity selection at fixed B yields lower risk at matched coverage than top-K.
datasets: Cached RIM-protocol queries with candidate lists, if a non-oracle gallery is obtained
experiment.config: B in {3,5}. Use a diversity weight picked on a held-out scene split before testing. Run 1000 scene-level bootstrap resamples.
experiment.success: Risk is lower by >=15% relative at 80% coverage, with a bootstrap CI excluding 0 for B=5, and set overlap with top-K is <0.8 so the selector is demonstrably distinct.
experiment.falsification: Stop if set overlap with top-K is >=0.9 or the risk gain is <5% relative; either means redundancy with the baseline.
experiment.compute: CPU, an estimated 3-8 hours if matcher outputs for the top-20 are cached. Not measured, and it would be blocked otherwise.
